title: Forge 3: a Linear layer with a hand-written backward

wrong.no_batch_sum.py: db takes the first example's gradient instead of summing over the batch
wrong.dx_no_transpose.py: dx = dout @ W instead of dout @ W.T (shape error unless W is square, wrong value even then)
wrong.dw_wrong_side.py: dW = dout.T @ x: the transpose of the right answer, shaped (out, in)
wrong.accumulates_grads.py: backward adds into dW and db, so a second call on the same batch doubles them (this lab's contract is SET)
wrong.aliases_input.py: the cache stores a reference to x, so a caller that reuses its buffer corrupts dW
wrong.only_2d.py: backward assumes 2-D inputs; (batch, time, features) inputs break dW and db
wrong.init_unscaled.py: W ~ Normal(0, 1) instead of Normal(0, 1/in_dim): activations explode with width
wrong.mean_over_batch.py: dW and db are averaged over the batch; that scaling belongs to the loss, not the layer

hints: Forward: y = x @ W + b. Cache x, because backward needs it. Copy it: the caller may overwrite its buffer.
Check shapes to get the three gradients: dW is (in, out) so it must be x.T @ dout; dx is (n, in) so it must be dout @ W.T; db is (out,) so it is dout summed over every non-feature axis.
The layer must NOT divide by the batch size: the loss already did (mean cross-entropy). For (batch, time, features) inputs, reshape x and dout to (-1, features) first, then the same two lines work.
Prove it with a finite-difference check: perturb one entry of W, recompute sum(upstream * forward(x)), and compare (L(w+e) - L(w-e)) / 2e with dW at that entry.
